correctness.rationale: For A SPD with distinct extreme eigenvalues 0<a<b, Gaussian S (s×N), s>=2 and post-sketch selected nonzero vector in the plane of extreme eigenvectors, the restricted Gram G^T G has positive determinant almost surely. The symmetric sketched denominator matrix H=diag(a,b)C symmetrized has positive diagonals and det H=ab C11 C22−(a+b)^2 C12^2/4; a negative eigenvalue occurs iff |C12|/sqrt(C11 C22)>rho*=2sqrt(ab)/(a+b). Gaussian columns are independent rotationally invariant, giving R²~Beta(1/2,(s−1)/2), so Pr(exists negative quotient)=I_{((b−a)/(b+a))²}((s−1)/2,1/2), specifically .4 for s=3,b/a=9. Deterministic Kantorovich spectral bound shows cosine(Av,v)>=rho* for all v; the operator-norm perturbation inequality ensures ⟨Av,Wv⟩>0 for SPD W with ||W−I||<rho*. The extremizing vector v=(sqrt(b/(a+b)),sqrt(a/(a+b))) in the extremes and a Householder reflector U with Uv=Av/||Av|| produce W=I−epsilon U SPD for epsilon<1, denominator zero at rho* and negative above it. This establishes sharpness and quantifier specificity. For N>2 the exact beta law is only for the extreme plane, not all vectors.
